mapping_keyed_diff.membership_reason: Approximate the residual medium-demersal reporting category using compatible source fish pools. Besides the existing coastal demersal guilds and Milkfish plus, include Carangids for its benthopelagic members and ML bathy for source-listed demersal Pontinus macrocephalus. Include Small pelagics because source-listed Lactarius lactarius schools over soft bottoms and eats bottom-living invertebrates/fishes (FAO printed2649). Guild names and provider size bins alone do not exclude these constituents. No measured residual composition establishes their caught fractions; mixed-pool membership remains Very low.

Interpret the provider Perch-likes/Medium demersals label as a historical fisheries reporting concept, with unknown constituent composition. Retain compatible L pisc comm, SM pisc, SM inv, L pisc and Carangids, and include Small pelagics because its source-listed Lactarius and Atropus are historical perciforms with coastal/bottom-associated ecology. FAO printed2649 explicitly places Lactariidae under Perciformes: Percoidei. Bathy examples are outside the historical order; modern classification of Pontinus does not establish historical residual membership. The eligible whole guilds contain other orders, so their catches proxy an assumed reporting mixture rather than measured perciform-only composition.

The residual pelagic label has no measured constituent composition. A1.3 explicitly includes deep-water fishes in S bathy/ML bathy, pelagic Naucrates ductor and Atule mate in SM pisc, Pampus and midwater fusiliers in SM inv, and Chanos in Milkfish plus. Include these compatible mixed pools alongside Small pelagics, Carangids, L pisc, Hilsa, Indian mackerel and Coastal scombrids. Source p17 calls SM guilds demersal/benthopelagic, so their pelagic-listed members support a disclosed mixed-guild approximation, not proof of the residual catch mixture. The provider medium-size tag is not an observed caught-size cutoff. Genuine source-zero S bathy remains eligible with weight zero.
